listening.title: Listening Part 1: joining a fitness centre
listening.instructions: Questions 1–10. Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. For questions 3, 8 and 10, choose A, B or C.
listening.voices: Receptionist (man) and Student (young woman); friendly conversation at a calm, clear pace
listening.transcript:
Receptionist: Good morning, Campus Fitness Centre.
Student: Hello. I'm a student and I'd like to ask about membership.
Receptionist: Of course. We have two types. Standard membership is thirty pounds a month and lets you use the gym and the swimming pool. Premium is forty-five pounds, and it includes fitness classes as well.
Student: I'm mainly interested in the classes. Which ones do you offer?
Receptionist: There's yoga on Mondays, dance on Wednesdays, and boxing on Saturday mornings.
Student: Dance sounds fun. What time is it?
Receptionist: It starts at half past six in the evening and lasts one hour.
Student: Perfect. Is there a discount for students?
Receptionist: Yes, students get twenty per cent off if they show a student card.
Student: That's great. Do I need to pay a joining fee?
Receptionist: Normally there's a one-off fee of ten pounds, but it's free this month.
Student: How long is the contract?
Receptionist: You can choose three months or twelve months.
Student: I'll take three months for now. Where can I sign up?
Receptionist: You can come to the reception desk any time before eight in the evening. Please bring your student card and a photo.
Student: Thank you. I'll come on Thursday.

questions.q: Standard membership: £______ a month
questions.why: Standard membership is thirty pounds a month.

questions.q: Premium membership: £______ a month
questions.why: Premium is forty-five pounds.

questions.q: What does Premium include that Standard does not?
questions.why: Premium includes fitness classes as well.

questions.q: Yoga class is on ______.
questions.why: There's yoga on Mondays.

questions.q: Dance class starts at ______ in the evening.
questions.why: It starts at half past six.

questions.q: The dance class lasts ______ hour.
questions.why: It lasts one hour.

questions.q: Students get ______ per cent off with a student card.
questions.why: Students get twenty per cent off.

questions.q: What is the joining fee this month?
questions.why: Normally ten pounds, but it's free this month.

questions.q: The student chooses a contract of ______ months.
questions.why: She says she'll take three months for now.

questions.q: What must she bring when she signs up?
options: A student card and a photo
questions.why: Please bring your student card and a photo.

listening.title: Listening Part 2: a new city bike scheme
listening.instructions: Questions 11–20. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C, or write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER where you see a line.
listening.voices: Speaker (man), one speaker; public talk at a steady pace
listening.transcript:
Speaker: Good evening, everyone. Tonight I'd like to tell you about the new bike scheme in our city, which starts next month.
Speaker: The idea is simple. There will be four hundred bikes at forty stations across the city. You take a bike from one station and leave it at any other station. The first thirty minutes of every journey are free, and after that it costs one pound for each extra half hour.
Speaker: To use the scheme, you must first register on the website or on the phone app. Registration is free, but you have to give your bank card details, because you pay a deposit of fifty pounds, which is returned if you stop using the bikes.
Speaker: Why is the council doing this? There are three main reasons. First, the centre of the city is very crowded, and the roads are often blocked. Second, many people cannot park near their work. And finally, the council wants people to be healthier.
Speaker: Safety is important. All the bikes have lights that work automatically, and helmets are for sale at some stations for five pounds. Riders under sixteen must wear a helmet, but for adults it is a recommendation, not a rule.
Speaker: The first stations will open near the railway station, the university and the main shopping street. The other stations will open over the next six months. If the scheme is a success, the council hopes to double the number of bikes within two years.
Speaker: Are there any questions?

questions.q: How many bikes will there be?
questions.why: There will be four hundred bikes.

questions.q: There will be ______ stations across the city.
questions.why: Four hundred bikes at forty stations.

questions.q: The first ______ minutes of every journey are free.
questions.why: The first thirty minutes are free.

questions.q: Each extra half hour costs £______.
questions.why: It costs one pound for each extra half hour.

questions.q: To register, people must use ...
options: the website or the phone app
questions.why: You must register on the website or on the phone app.

questions.q: The deposit is £______.
questions.why: You pay a deposit of fifty pounds.

questions.q: One reason for the scheme is that ...
options: the roads in the centre are crowded
questions.why: The centre is very crowded and the roads are often blocked.

questions.q: Who must wear a helmet?
questions.why: Riders under sixteen must wear a helmet.

questions.q: The first stations will open near the railway station, the university and the main ______ street.
questions.why: The main shopping street.

questions.q: If the scheme is a success, the council hopes to ...
questions.why: It hopes to double the number of bikes within two years.

reading.title: Reading Passage 1: the rise of the podcast
reading.instructions: Questions 21–24: Do the statements agree with the information in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Questions 25–27: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Questions 28–30: Complete the sentences. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.
reading.passage:
The Rise of the Podcast

Twenty years ago, hardly anyone had heard the word 'podcast'. Today, millions of people listen to them every week, on their way to work, while they cook, or during a long walk. A podcast is simply a series of audio programmes that can be downloaded from the internet and played whenever the listener likes.

One reason for this growth is the cost. Making a podcast needs very little equipment: a microphone, a computer and some free software are enough. As a result, almost anyone with an interesting idea can start one, and this has produced shows on subjects as different as cooking, history, football and mental health. Unlike radio stations, podcasters do not need a licence from the government.

Another reason is convenience. Listeners decide when and where to listen, and they can stop and start as they wish. Many people say that podcasts are better than television, because they can do other things while they listen. A recent survey found that one third of listeners hear their favourite shows while driving, and another quarter listen while doing housework.

Not everything about podcasts is positive, however. Because anyone can make one, the quality varies greatly, and some podcasts give information that is not correct. Making money is also difficult. Most small podcasts earn little or nothing, so the people who make them usually have other jobs. Only a small number earn enough from advertising to become full-time podcasters.

Despite these problems, experts expect the number of listeners to continue growing, especially among young people, who are now the largest group.

questions.q: A podcast can be played at any time the listener chooses.
questions.why: It can be played whenever the listener likes.

questions.q: Podcasters need a licence from the government.
questions.why: Unlike radio stations, podcasters do not need a licence.

questions.q: Podcasts about football are the most popular.
questions.why: The passage does not say which subject is most popular.

questions.q: Most podcasters earn enough to work full-time.
questions.why: Only a small number earn enough to become full-time podcasters.

questions.q: What is needed to make a podcast?
options: A microphone, a computer and free software
questions.why: A microphone, a computer and some free software are enough.

questions.q: What does the survey say about driving?
options: One third of listeners hear their favourite shows while driving
questions.why: One third of listeners hear their favourite shows while driving.

questions.q: Which group of listeners is now the largest?
questions.why: Young people are now the largest group.

questions.q: Podcasts can be about subjects such as cooking, history, football and ______.
questions.why: The subjects include mental health.

questions.q: The ______ of podcasts varies greatly.
questions.why: The quality varies greatly.

questions.q: A small number of podcasters earn enough from ______ to work full-time.
questions.why: Only a small number earn enough from advertising.

reading.title: Reading Passage 2: starting again at forty
reading.instructions: Questions 31–34: Do the statements agree with the information in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Questions 35–37: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. Questions 38–40: Complete the sentences. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage.
reading.passage:
Starting Again at Forty

When Rosa Martinez turned forty, she did something that surprised her friends and family: she left her job as an accountant and began studying to become a nurse. 'I had worked in an office for sixteen years,' she says, 'and I was never really happy. One day I looked at the list of things I wanted to do in life, and I realised that I had not done any of them.'

Rosa's decision was not easy. She had to pay for her course herself, and her husband was worried about money. To save, the family sold their second car and stopped going on holiday abroad. Rosa also found studying difficult at first, because it was twenty years since she had last been in a classroom. 'The other students were half my age,' she remembers. 'In the first week I felt like their mother.'

Luckily, her classmates turned out to be very friendly. They helped her with the computer programs she was not familiar with, and in return she gave them advice on managing their time and money. She also found that her experience at work was useful. 'In an office you learn to stay calm when people are angry with you,' she says. 'That is exactly what you need in a hospital.'

Three years later, Rosa finished her studies and now works in a children's ward. She earns less than she did as an accountant, but she says she has never regretted her choice. 'Every morning I look forward to going to work,' she says. 'I could not say that before.'

Her advice to others who are thinking about changing career? 'Do not wait too long. And do not be afraid of being the oldest person in the room.'

questions.q: Rosa worked as an accountant for sixteen years.
questions.why: She had worked in an office for sixteen years.

questions.q: Rosa's husband was happy about her decision from the start.
questions.why: Her husband was worried about money.

questions.q: Rosa has two children.
questions.why: Her children are not mentioned.

questions.q: Rosa now earns more money than she did before.
questions.why: She earns less than she did as an accountant.

questions.q: How did the family save money?
options: They moved to a smaller house
questions.why: The family sold their second car.

questions.q: How did Rosa feel in her first week as a student?
options: Like the mother of the other students
questions.why: In the first week she felt like their mother.

questions.q: How did her classmates help her?
questions.why: They helped her with the computer programs.

questions.q: In her office job, Rosa learned to stay ______ when people were angry.
questions.why: In an office you learn to stay calm.

questions.q: Rosa now works in a children's ______.
questions.why: She works in a children's ward.

questions.q: Her advice is: 'Do not ______ too long.'
questions.why: Do not wait too long.

writing.stem: The table below shows the percentage of people who used five types of transport to travel to work in one town in 2010 and in 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 100 words.
writing.chartFacts: Percentage of people using five types of transport to travel to work in one town. Car: 55 in 2010, 48 in 2020. Bus: 20, 17. Bicycle: 5, 14. Walking: 15, 16. Train: 5, 5. Key features: the car was the most common way to travel in both years but fell from 55% to 48%; the bicycle showed the biggest increase, almost tripling from 5% to 14%; bus use fell from 20% to 17%; walking rose slightly from 15% to 16%; train use stayed the same at 5%.
